name: PC (constraint-based)
tagline: Classical constraint-based causal discovery: chi-squared CI tests on discrete data, then collider/Meek orientation.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize complete undirected graph $G$ over $X_1,\dots,X_d$
2. Stable skeleton: for increasing $|S|$, remove edge $(i,j)$ if $\chi^2$ test gives $X_i \perp X_j \mid S$ at $\alpha = 0.05$
3. Orient unshielded triples $i - k - j$ as colliders $i \to k \leftarrow j$ when $k \notin \text{sepset}(i,j)$
4. Apply Meek rules to propagate edge orientations
5. Return resulting CPDAG
diff_from_baseline: Spirtes, Glymour & Scheines, 'Causation, Prediction, and Search' (2000). Uses causal-learn's stable PC with chi-squared CI tests for discrete data and UC-sepset + Meek orientation. Default constraint-based reference for discrete causal discovery.

name: GES (score-based)
tagline: Greedy Equivalence Search over CPDAGs using BDeu score with two phases: forward edge additions then backward deletions.
pseudocode:
1. Start from empty CPDAG; cache local BDeu scores
2. Forward Equivalence Search: greedily add the edge that maximizes the BDeu score increase
3. Repeat until no addition improves the score
4. Backward Equivalence Search: greedily delete the edge that maximizes the score increase
5. Repeat until no deletion improves the score
6. Return final CPDAG
diff_from_baseline: Chickering, 'Optimal structure identification with greedy search' (JMLR 2002). Two-phase greedy search in CPDAG space using BDeu (Bayesian Dirichlet equivalent uniform) score; the canonical score-based reference for discrete Bayesian network learning.

name: GRaSP (permutation-based)
tagline: Greedy Relaxation of the Sparsest Permutation algorithm: searches over orderings with depth-bounded DFS to find a low-score DAG.
pseudocode:
1. Start from a random permutation $\pi$ of variables
2. For each variable, project onto $\pi$ to get DAG with parents preceding the node
3. Score the DAG via local BDeu and cache scores
4. Run depth-3 DFS over swaps in $\pi$, accepting swaps that lower total score
5. Repeat until no admissible swap exists at any depth
6. Convert final DAG to its CPDAG
diff_from_baseline: Lam, Andrews & Ramsey, 'Greedy Relaxations of the Sparsest Permutation Algorithm' (UAI 2022). Permutation-based search with depth-3 DFS relaxation over orderings, using BDeu score for discrete data; achieves strong recovery on dense graphs.

name: BOSS (best-order search)
tagline: Best Order Score Search: greedily reorders variables and uses Grow-Shrink trees to score parent sets, returning the best DAG over orderings.
pseudocode:
1. Start from a random permutation $\pi$
2. For each variable, fit Grow-Shrink parent sets within prefix of $\pi$ scored by BDeu
3. Iterate over swaps and reinsertions of each node into $\pi$ to lower total score
4. Accept the move that maximally decreases the score
5. Repeat until $\pi$ is locally optimal
6. Convert the implied DAG to its CPDAG
diff_from_baseline: Andrews, Ramsey, Sanchez Romero, Camchong & Velasquez, 'Fast Scalable and Accurate Discovery of DAGs Using the Best Order Score Search and Grow-Shrink Trees' (NeurIPS 2023). State-of-the-art permutation-based score search; the strongest causal-learn permutation reference.

name: Hill Climbing (greedy DAG)
tagline: Greedy DAG hill-climbing in BDeu score space using add/delete/reverse edge operators with cycle checks; convert to CPDAG at the end.
pseudocode:
1. Start with empty adjacency $A$; cache $s_j = \text{BDeu}(j, \emptyset)$ for each node $j$
2. For every ordered pair $(i,j)$, compute score delta of ADD / DELETE / REVERSE under DAG cycle constraint
3. Pick the operator with the largest score improvement $\Delta > 0$
4. Apply it and refresh local scores for affected nodes
5. Repeat until no admissible move improves the score
6. Convert the learned DAG to its CPDAG via dag2cpdag
diff_from_baseline: Heckerman, Geiger & Chickering, 'Learning Bayesian networks: the combination of knowledge and statistical data' (Mach. Learn. 1995). Classic greedy DAG hill-climbing with add/delete/reverse moves and BDeu score; widely used baseline that often gets stuck in local optima but is computationally cheap.
